mappings.note: Taatparya of 'vajra chhipa', keyed to the literal lightning hidden in the clouds. Not LO-7: the symbolic option is not the key, so only comprehension is rewarded. (Duplicate of 745fa032 -- reported, not fixed.)
Recall of the names the poet calls the clouds by -- all of the above. Not LO-7: the epithets only have to be recognised as the poem's, not explained.
Explicitly asks the prateekaatmak roop of the cloud (kraanti aur paurush). Not LO-6: the literal cloud is not the answer, the bhaav behind the pratik is.
'Dharaadhar kiske liye prayukt hua hai' -- the referent of the poet's epithet, same treatment as ab2050be. Not LO-6: it asks about usage in the poem, not a dictionary gloss.
What the poet prays the clouds for -- stated content, keyed 'all of the above'. Not LO-7: relief from the heat is the poem's letter; the saanketik reading sits on other items.

Asks WHY the clouds are called 'anant ke ghan' -- explanation of the poet's expression. Not LO-6: 09faa7d1 already covers the plain 'where do they come from' fact; this needs the reasoning behind the phrase.
Asks the prateekaatmak bhaav of 'jal' (shaanti and sukh). Not LO-6: the literal rainfall is the distractor.
Which collection is NOT Nirala's -- bibliography. Mapped at competency level because the frame has no biography/literary-history LO. Not LO-6: no prescribed poem is read to answer it.

The options are verse forms (muktak vs rola/soratha/doha); what is tested is the kaavya-roop Nirala writes in. Not C-H1.3: the substance is a poetic upaadaan, which LO-2 names, not a fact of the poet's life.
Which kaavya-dhaara Nirala belongs to (Chhaayaavaad) -- literary history. Not LO-7: no line of the poem is being appreciated, only the movement is named.
The upamaan for the clouds' beauty (kaale ghunghraale baal). Not LO-5: the stem does not name or ask for an alankaar, it asks what the comparison is with.
The upamaan in 'baal kalpana ke-se paale'. Not LO-5: no alankaar is named or to be identified; the comparison's term is what is scored.
What the poet calls the clouds (navjeevan vaale) -- recall. Not LO-7: fcf318a3 and 8f8f8b5e take the 'in what sense / why' versions of the same epithet.
Into what the poet asks nootan kavita to be poured -- comprehension of the line's referent. Not LO-7: the answer is the addressee, not the bhaav of the line.
What Phagun puts on people's faces -- content. Not LO-7: e1f942bc takes the manahsthiti reading of Phagun's effect; here only the stated fact is wanted.
Which month brings greenery everywhere -- content. Not C-H1.1: the passage is the prescribed poem, not apathit material.

Asks who wrote 'At nahin rahi hai' -- authorship, i.e. literary identification, mapped at the competency because the frame has no biography LO. Not LO-6: no content of the poem is involved. (Nirala is absent from the options and the key is wrong -- reported, not fixed.)
Which maas the poem describes -- content. Not LO-7: no saundarya explanation is asked.
What it is that is not 'at' rahi -- comprehension of the title line. Not LO-7: the answer restates the poem, it does not interpret the image.
What fills every house -- content. Not LO-7: nothing symbolic has to be unpacked.
What the quoted lines describe (praakritik saundarya) -- comprehension. Not LO-7: it asks the subject of the description, not its kala-paksh.
Name the paath and its poet from the padyaansh -- identification of text and author. Not LO-6: no content question about the poem is asked, only its literary identity.
What happens to the branches when Phagun arrives -- content. Not LO-7: the imagery is reported, not explained.
What the poet means by 'pat nahin rahi hai' -- paraphrase of the line. Not LO-7: the keyed answer is the plain sense (beauty everywhere), not a saundarya-bodh vyaakhyaa.
Describe the natural beauty of Phagun in your own words, on the basis of the poem -- a kaavyabodh answer restating the poem's content. Not LO-7: it asks what the poem depicts, not how it depicts it.
Why 'garjan' rather than fuhaar/rimjhim, with reasons -- the poet's choice of ojas and the kraanti bhaav. Not LO-6: the contrast forces an explanation of bhaav-paksh, not recall.
WHY the cloud is likened to children's imagination -- explanation of the upamaan. Not LO-5: the stem names no alankaar and wants the reasoning, not identification.
What the poet means by 'vidyut-chhabi ur mein, kavi navjeevan vaale' -- vyaakhyaa of a line's bhaav. Not LO-6: 2d7f5adc holds the recall version of the same image.
What kind of rachnaa Utsaah is -- its kaavya-roop (aahvaan geet in mukt chhand). Not LO-7: the question is about form and medium, not about saundarya or bhaav.
'Nav jeevan vaale' kis ko kahaa gayaa hai aur kyon -- the referent pattern plus its justification. Not LO-6: 7ad25b76 covers the plain recall; here the reason must be explained.

Why Nirala asks the cloud to thunder rather than rain -- bhaav-paksh reasoning. Not LO-6: the barasnaa/garjnaa contrast cannot be answered by recall. (Near-duplicate of 020b5e8d -- reported, not fixed.)
Describe Phagun's natural splendour in your own words -- restating the poem's content. Not LO-7: no kala-paksh or shilp analysis is demanded. (Near-duplicate of 5d1e6b06 -- reported, not fixed.)
The sandesh of 'At nahin rahi hai' -- the poem's central bhaav. Not LO-6: a theme statement is not answerable by pointing at a line.
Who were vikal and unman, and why -- who/why comprehension of a stated line. Not LO-7: the poem gives the cause (the heat) directly.
Vyaakhyaa of 'vidyut-chhavi ur mein, kavi navjeevan vaale' -- the line's bhaav. Not LO-6: it asks the meaning intended, not the wording. (Duplicate of 4f511ae4 -- reported, not fixed.)
How Phagun affects people's minds, in the light of a quoted line -- manahsthiti and bhaav-paksh. Not LO-6: the line has to be interpreted, not reported.
Which ritu is described and what it is that will not fit -- two content facts. Not LO-7: no explanation of the image is required.
What Phagun's aabhaa is like and how the poem states its condition -- comprehension of what the poem says. Not LO-7: it asks the described state, not an appreciation of how it is crafted.
What the poet wants to do on seeing the beauty around -- stated content. Not LO-7: the poem answers it directly, no bhaav has to be inferred.
